![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14167856/assets/fe1b1b8f9837ec2fbd6a7eab48b7f4575dd0e247b6d633ec5e440b43f5efc04f.png)

The line shown above passes through the points $(0,6)$ and $(5,2).$ What is the equation of the line?
question.worked_solution:
We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form $y=mx+b.$ So we need to work out the slope $m$ and the $y$-intercept $b.$

From the graph, we see that the line intercepts the $y$-axis at $(0,6).$ So, the $y$-intercept is $b=6.$

We can calculate the slope of the line by choosing two points on the line and applying the slope formula. The line passes through the points $(0,6)$ and $(5,2),$ so we calculate its slope as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{2-6}{5-0} \\  & =\frac{-4}{5} \\  & =-\frac{4}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the slope $m=-\frac{4}{5}$ and the $y$-intercept $b=6$ into the slope-intercept form $y=mx+b,$ we obtain the equation of the line:

$$
y=-\frac{4}{5}x+6
$$
